To discuss the latest developments, we are joined by Al Jazeera correspondents Sinem Koseoglu in Tehran and Aksel Zaimovic in Doha.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Sudan's army is working to consolidate control of the strategic al-Sadirat, or Exports Road, linking Khartoum with el-Obeid and the wider Kordofan and Darfur regions. 
The route was controlled by the Rapid Support Forces for much of Sudan's three-year conflict before the army recaptured it last month, along with several towns and cities. Burnt vehicles, abandoned buildings and deserted communities along the highway reveal the scale of the fighting. 
Jabrat al-Sheikh, one of the largest towns along the route, has become a ghost town after fierce battles drove civilians away. 
The army is continuing operations to regain territory, while the RSF continues drone attacks on army-controlled areas in Kordofan. Hundreds of thousands of displaced people are still waiting to find out when they can safely return home.

Al Jazeera's Hiba Morgan reports from Jabrat al-Sheikh in North Kordofan.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The Trump administration is ramping up economic pressure on Iran while threatening military strikes. In an interview with Al Jazeera, former US ambassador Joey Hood said President Trump has "clearly understood the limits" of military strikes but warned that Iran is "not going to suddenly change its behaviour" in response to sanctions. He noted that it took two years of sanctions to bring Iran to the negotiating table for the 2015 nuclear deal, but that China and Russia are not "fully on board" now, and Iran knows the president is "after regime change", making a similar outcome unlikely. Hood said he does not see a diplomatic off-ramp under Trump, but suggested a future US president could offer one. He proposed an "Islamic naval coalition led by Pakistan, Turkey" to monitor the Strait of Hormuz and allow both sides to back away from the conflict while saving face.
